messages:
ana_fin: Heads-up — can we do a quick pass on the GPU daily alert thresholds? infra-cost-bot spammed the channel overnight with 3 low-priority alerts and it drowned out a real surge alert.

beth_finops: ugh sorry I missed that. Do we have the raw numbers? which projects triggered?

mike_cloudops: I pulled the export. Looks like two alerts came from preemptible test pools for team-alpha and one from an experimental customer sim workload. total dev spend yesterday spiked to $2.1k but sustained was ~1.2k.

infra-cost-bot: ALERT: daily_gpu_spend > 95% threshold for project: team-alpha-preemptible (value: $730, threshold: $700) :warning:

ana_fin (typo) — ignore

dev_platform: (cc @beth_finops @mike_cloudops) we should treat preemptible pools differently — smaller thresholds and higher noise tolerance. Proposal: set per-tag thresholds and only escalate if 3+ distinct projects breach within 6h.

beth_finops: I like per-tag thresholds. Right now thresholds are global: `daily_gpu = $700` per project. That was a quick default. If we switch to tag-based we need a fallback for untagged resources.

mike_cloudops: Agreed. We can implement rule set in the alerting engine. Rough plan:
```
if resource.tag == "preemptible": threshold = base * 0.6
elif resource.tag == "customer-experiment": threshold = base * 1.5
else: threshold = base
```
Plus: require `count(distinct project) >= 3` for channel-level paging.

ana_fin (again typo) — ignore

beth_finops: Action items: 1) create tag whitelist + owners, 2) patch alert engine to support tag thresholds, 3) backfill alerts for last 30 days to tune multipliers. Assigning owners: @mike_cloudops for patch, @dev_platform for backfill script, @beth_finops to validate numbers with finance.

dev_platform: I'll spin up a backfill query in BigQuery. Query snippet:
```
SELECT project_id, SUM(gpu_cost) as daily_gpu_cost
FROM `redwood-billing.gcp_usage.gpu_daily`
WHERE usage_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY project_id
ORDER BY daily_gpu_cost DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

mike_cloudops: ETA for alert engine change: 48hrs. Will add unit tests and a flag to revert if too noisy.

beth_finops: Also let's add per-customer budget views in the finance dashboard. Right now customers using dedicated pools don't show up cleanly. I'll open a ticket to map customer IDs to billing projects.

ana_fin — STOP — (ignore typos)

infra-cost-bot: INFO: created incident 2027-11-05-909 for noisy-alerts channel suppression (auto).

ana_fin: 😂 can we also suppress bot pings between 00:00-06:00 PT unless severity >= high? Night noise is killing on-call.

dev_platform: Good call. I'll add a schedule window and an override for severity. Also adding a metric to track "alerts muted but exceeded" so we don't hide real issues.

beth_finops: For reconciliation: once backfill is done, I'll run a quick script to recompute allocated spend and see if tagging drift caused mis-attribution last month. If we find orphaned charges, we'll reassign to owner teams before the next invoice.

mike_cloudops: One more: adjust alert text to include `billing_link` and `top 3 processes` that consumed GPUs. Makes triage faster.

beth_finops: Sounds good. I'll follow up with a short playbook for on-call steps when a true GPU surge hits.

ana_fin: Thanks all. Quick check-in tomorrow 10am PT?

mike_cloudops: 10am works for me.

dev_platform: Works.

beth_finops: Saved.

infra-cost-bot: NOTE: next scheduled noisy-alerts suppression window 00:00-06:00 PT enabled.
